en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, scientifically named Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and is critically endangered due to severe habitat deforestation.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, is the highest court and heads the judicial branch of government.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago using stone walls.
The Philippine national flag features a white triangle with three gold stars representing the major island groups of Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Dr. Fe del Mundo was the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School and invented a bamboo incubator for rural hospitals.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a two-step forward, one-step backward dance mimicking a river current.
Baybayin is an ancient pre-colonial Philippine writing system where each character represents a syllable, like the letter a or ba.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, citizens who are at least eighteen years old have the right to vote in national elections.
The sampaguita, scientifically known as Jasminum sambac, is the national flower of the Philippines and symbolizes purity and simplicity.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition for his massive historical painting Spoliarium.
